key_insight: The model segmented vertebral and vascular structures very accurately, but adding the segmentation did not improve—and actually reduced—reader diagnostic accuracy for vertebral artery dissection on CTA.
clinical_relevance: This suggests segmentation-based CTA enhancement is promising for visualization, but it is not yet reliable enough to support routine diagnosis of vertebral artery dissection in acute care.
method: Retrospective study with internal training data and an external test cohort.
Trained a nnU-Net v2 vascular segmentation model using five-fold cross-validation.
Ran a two-part crossover reader study with 10 readers comparing CTA with vs without augmentation.
evidence_signal: The model achieved a Dice similarity coefficient of 0.96 ± 0.01, but reader accuracy was lower with augmentation than without (0.72 vs 0.84; P < .001).
watch_item: High segmentation accuracy did not translate into better clinical reading performance, so external validation and workflow testing are still needed before implementation.
paper_title: Does Deep Learning Vascular Segmentation on CTA Improve Vertebral Artery Dissection Detection?
